note: Second Life LSL vehicle reference. Values copied from wiki.secondlife.com (rendered pages) on 2026-11-10 and cross-checked against Linden Lab's lsl-definitions on GitHub. Where the wiki's own pages disagree, both readings are kept in 'disputes'. [checked 2026-11-10]
warning: The wiki says of the type defaults: they are not the optimal settings and will change; do not rely on them staying constant. Set every parameter your vehicle depends on.

type_notes.sled: no motor of its own: slides, good for gravity-driven things
type_notes.car: ground vehicle: strong sideways friction, stays upright, will not motor into the sky
type_notes.boat: hovers on water, mild banking, gentle friction
type_notes.airplane: banks into turns, needs speed to turn, no hover
type_notes.balloon: full buoyancy, hovers 5 m up, slow and floaty

time to align the up axis with world up
vector_params: decay time of linear velocity along the vehicle's x, y, z axes
decay time of angular velocity about the vehicle's x, y, z axes
linear velocity the vehicle tries to reach, in its own frame
angular velocity the vehicle tries to reach, in its own frame
capped at 4*PI rad/s (two turns a second)

rotation of the vehicle's axes relative to the root prim (set with llSetVehicleRotationParam)
flags: no linear deflection along world z: stops ground vehicles climbing into the sky
the vertical attractor limits roll only, so the vehicle can climb and dive

limits: Linear motor: clamped to about 30 m/s.
Angular motor: capped at 4*PI rad/s, two turns a second.
Motor decay timescales: capped at 120 s, and always on.
Timescales: the minimum is about a tenth of a second (0.07 for the friction vectors); zero is safe and means the minimum.
To switch a behaviour off, give it a very large timescale: 300 or more.
Hover: on only when VEHICLE_HOVER_TIMESCALE is under 300 s; it works over terrain and water, not over prims.
Vertical attractor: off when its timescale is above 500 s. Banking needs it on.
A motor set to ZERO_VECTOR actively brakes to zero; a motor left to decay just stops pushing.
If a motor's decay timescale is shorter than its timescale, the motor never reaches its full value.
Physics weight: a scripted vehicle may weigh at most 32.0; above that llSetVehicleType fails with a debug-channel warning.
One vehicle behaviour per object. Setting the type resets every parameter to that type's defaults.
Axes: local +x is forward, +y is left, +z is up, on the root prim. If the build disagrees, set VEHICLE_REFERENCE_FRAME.
Mono script memory 64 KB; the event queue holds 64 events and drops the rest silently.
caveats: Do not mix vehicle behaviour with llSetBuoyancy, llSetForce, llSetTorque or llSetHoverHeight; do not use llGroundRepel with vehicles.
llSetPos and llSetRot do nothing to a physical root prim, and each costs a 0.2 s forced delay.
Setting the type does not take controls or move anything, but a physical vehicle parked on a slope will slide: keep physics off until someone drives.
Some flags can survive a script reset: remove the flags you do not want with llRemoveVehicleFlags.
Setting STATUS_PHYSICS fails silently on attachments.
The hover centre is the centre of mass, and it moves when avatars sit.
One script is better than many: use llSetLinkPrimitiveParamsFast for wheels and lights rather than a script per prim.
Permissions: ask for all of them in one llRequestPermissions call, OR-ed together; a later call that leaves one out drops it.
Seated avatars are auto-granted take-controls, trigger-animation, track-camera and control-camera, but the wiki says not to rely on it: do the work in run_time_permissions.
A script holds permissions for one avatar at a time.
llTakeControls(controls, TRUE, FALSE) is the vehicle form: the keys raise control events and stop moving the avatar.
Camera permission and scripted camera settings are cleared automatically when the avatar stands.
CHANGED_REGION is raised only in the root prim. The crossing triggers when the root prim's centre is a metre past the border.
Region corners and very high speed can start a second crossing before the first finishes; results are poor. Slow down at corners.
The wiki gives no official scripting recipe for crossings. Common practice, not Linden guidance: after CHANGED_REGION, set the camera parameters again and restart the driving animation.
disputes: VEHICLE_HOVER_HEIGHT maximum: the tutorial says 100 m; a 2010 server note mentions values above 1024 misbehaving. The current maximum is not verified.
VEHICLE_BUOYANCY range: the tables say -1 to 1, the tutorial says 0 to 1. Linden's definitions say -1 to 1.
VEHICLE_BANKING_EFFICIENCY: an open bug report says negative values behave like positive ones.
CAMERA_DISTANCE range: the table says 0.5 to 50, an example on the same page says 0.5 to 10.
controls: strafe left: Shift-left or Shift-A (left or A in mouselook)
strafe right: Shift-right or Shift-D (right or D in mouselook)
turn left: left arrow or A
turn right: right arrow or D
control_event: control(key id, integer level, integer edge): level = keys down now, edge = keys that changed.
just pressed = level & edge; just released = ~level & edge; still held = level & ~edge.
delays: llSetVehicle* functions, llSitTarget, llTakeControls, llSetCameraParams, llSetTimerEvent, llSetStatus
none, but the 64-event queue drops overflow silently
